stem.en: Management is the process of getting things done with the aim of achieving goals:

explanation.en: The definition covers both: reaching the goal (effectiveness) with the least use of resources (efficiency).

stem.en: Effectiveness in management is concerned with:

options.en: doing the right task and achieving the goal on time
doing the task at the minimum cost
lowering the labour cost per unit
reducing the wastage of raw material

explanation.en: Effectiveness is about the end result: completing the right job on time. The other options describe efficiency.

stem.en: A firm produced its full target output on time, but its cost of production rose sharply because of wastage. The firm is:

explanation.en: The target was met on time (effective) but resources were wasted (not efficient).

stem.en: Efficiency in management mainly refers to:

options.en: the relationship between output and the resources (inputs) used

explanation.en: Efficiency is a cost-benefit idea: more output for the same input, or the same output with less input.

stem.en: Management is said to be all-pervasive because:

options.en: it is needed only in large companies
it is needed in all types of organisations, economic, social and political, in every country
it is done only by top managers
it can be seen and touched

explanation.en: Management is universal: schools, hospitals, shops and governments all need it.

stem.en: Survival, profit and growth are the ___ objectives of management.

explanation.en: These three are the organisational objectives that keep the business alive and expanding.

stem.en: Management cannot be seen, but its presence is felt in the results. This characteristic is called:

explanation.en: Management is an intangible force: we see its effect in order, output and satisfaction.

stem.en: A fast-food chain changes its menu to suit local tastes when it opens outlets in a new state. Which characteristic of management does this show?

explanation.en: Changing to suit the environment shows that management is a dynamic function.

stem.en: Using environment-friendly methods of production and giving jobs to disadvantaged sections of society are examples of:

explanation.en: Benefits created for society are social objectives.

stem.en: Management is not a full-fledged profession mainly because:

options.en: there is no restricted entry; no compulsory degree or licence is needed to be a manager
it is not taught in colleges
it has no body of knowledge

explanation.en: Unlike medicine or law, anyone can become a manager without a prescribed qualification.

stem.en: Principles of management are not as exact as the laws of physics because:

options.en: they are not based on any experimentation
they deal with human behaviour, which is hard to predict

explanation.en: Human behaviour varies, so management is called an inexact (soft) science.

stem.en: Personalised application of knowledge, based on practice and creativity, is a feature of management as:

explanation.en: Personal skill and creativity in applying knowledge are features of an art.

stem.en: Practising managers are not required to be members of any body such as the All India Management Association. On which feature of a profession does management therefore fall short?

explanation.en: A true profession requires membership of a professional association; for managers it is optional.

stem.en: Which statement about the nature of management is correct?

options.en: It is neither an art nor a science
It is a full-fledged profession like medicine
It is an exact science like physics
It is an art, an inexact science, and has some but not all features of a profession

explanation.en: Management satisfies the features of art, partly those of science, and only some features of a profession.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Management is a full-fledged profession.
Reason (R): Management has a well-defined, systematised body of knowledge.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Management has a body of knowledge (R is true), but it lacks restricted entry and compulsory membership of a professional body, so it is not a full profession (A is false).

stem.en: Which level of management formulates the overall objectives and strategies of an organisation?

explanation.en: Top management sets the goals, strategies and policies for the whole organisation.

stem.en: A foreman in a factory belongs to:

explanation.en: Foremen are in direct contact with workers: the supervisory level.

stem.en: Interpreting the policies framed by top management is a function of:

explanation.en: Middle managers translate top-level policies into departmental plans.

stem.en: Which of these is NOT a function of supervisory management?

options.en: Passing on workers' problems to higher levels
Analysing the business environment and its effect on the survival of the firm

explanation.en: Analysing the environment for the firm's survival is a top-management function.

stem.en: At which level of management does Imran work?

explanation.en: Imran is in direct contact with workers, checks quality and passes on their grievances: supervisory level.

passage.en: Rohan Electricals makes ceiling fans. The managing director has set a target of selling 2 lakh fans this year. The production head, Ms Kavya, planned the output of each plant and allotted machines. At the plant, supervisor Imran checks the quality of every batch and passes the workers' complaints about heat on the shop floor to Ms Kavya. Last quarter the plant made 60,000 fans, but the sales team sold only 45,000.

stem.en: Deciding in advance what to do and how to do it is called:

explanation.en: Planning bridges the gap between where we are and where we want to be.

stem.en: Monitoring performance against standards and taking corrective action is:

explanation.en: Controlling compares actual results with standards and corrects deviations.

stem.en: Finding the right people for the right jobs is the function of:

explanation.en: Staffing fills positions with suitable people.

stem.en: Assigning duties, grouping tasks, establishing authority and allocating resources is called:

explanation.en: This is the definition of organising.

stem.en: The production manager of a cycle factory compares the actual output of 9,000 cycles with the target of 10,000 and asks supervisors to find the reasons. Which function is being performed?

explanation.en: Measuring actual output against a target and looking for causes of deviation is controlling.

stem.en: Coordination is called the essence of management because:

options.en: it is needed at every level and in every function to integrate efforts
it is a separate function done only by top managers
it is needed only when there is a conflict
it is needed only in planning

explanation.en: Coordination runs through all functions and levels, so it is the essence of management, not a separate function.

stem.en: Coordination is a ___ function, because a manager must coordinate consciously even when people are willing to cooperate.

explanation.en: Cooperation is voluntary, but coordination must be done deliberately by managers.

stem.en: Which of the following is NOT a feature of coordination?

options.en: It is the responsibility of top management only

explanation.en: Coordination is the responsibility of managers at all levels, not only the top.

stem.en: As an organisation grows in size and employs more specialists, the need for coordination:

explanation.en: Growth, functional differentiation and specialisation all increase the need for coordination.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Coordination is the essence of management.
Reason (R): Coordination is required at all levels of management and in all its functions.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true, and because coordination runs through every level and function, it is called the essence of management.

stem.en: The gap between fans made and fans sold points mainly to a lack of:

explanation.en: Production and sales did not synchronise their activities: 15,000 fans remained unsold.

passage.en: Rohan Electricals makes ceiling fans. The managing director has set a target of selling 2 lakh fans this year. The production head, Ms Kavya, planned the output of each plant and allotted machines. At the plant, supervisor Imran checks the quality of every batch and passes the workers' complaints about heat on the shop floor to Ms Kavya. Last quarter the plant made 60,000 fans, but the sales team sold only 45,000.

stem.en: A company met its production target of 10,000 units on time, but used 20% more raw material than the standard allowed. The company is:

explanation.en: The target was achieved on time, so the company was effective; but it used more input than necessary for that output, so it was not efficient.

stem.en: Which feature of a profession is NOT found in management?

options.en: Restricted entry through a compulsory examination or degree

explanation.en: Anyone can be appointed a manager without a compulsory degree or licence, so management lacks restricted entry. The other features are present in management.

stem.en:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) Coordination is needed in all departments and at all levels (B) Coordination needs conscious effort by managers (C) Coordination begins at planning and lasts till controlling
List II: (i) Deliberate function (ii) Continuous process (iii) All-pervasive

explanation.en: Needed everywhere = all-pervasive; needs conscious effort = deliberate function; runs from planning to controlling = continuous process.
